description: Lay-language phrases mapped to HPO terms. Curated by Peter's Kiro from development-split notes only (never held-out notes). Each entry was checked against the stored JAX record and given a rationale. 'verified' means: HP id and official name confirmed, and the phrase plainly describes the phenotype. It does not mean clinically validated.

entries.label: Hypotonia

source.sourcePhrase: very floppy

entries.rationale: 'Floppy' is the common lay word for low muscle tone; HPO lists 'Low muscle tone' as a synonym.

entries.label: Hypotonia

source.sourcePhrase: very floppy

entries.rationale: Short form of the same wording.

entries.label: Cryptorchidism

source.sourcePhrase: both testicles had not come down

entries.rationale: Undescended testes is the definition of cryptorchidism.

entries.label: Cryptorchidism

source.sourcePhrase: both testicles had not come down

entries.rationale: Common everyday wording of the same finding.

entries.label: Poor suck

source.sourcePhrase: he sucked weakly

entries.rationale: Direct description of a weak suck.

entries.label: Failure to thrive

source.sourcePhrase: He kept growing poorly as a baby

entries.rationale: Poor infant growth is the core of failure to thrive.

entries.label: Failure to thrive

source.sourcePhrase: has not been gaining weight

entries.rationale: HPO search for 'poor weight gain' returns Failure to thrive first; accepted for infants and children only.

entries.label: Polyphagia

source.sourcePhrase: started eating all the time

entries.rationale: Excessive eating; HPO search for 'hyperphagia' resolves to Polyphagia.

entries.phrase: carried a lot of body fat
entries.label: Obesity

source.sourcePhrase: carried a lot of body fat

entries.rationale: Plain description of excess body fat.

entries.label: Short stature

source.sourcePhrase: shorter than nearly all boys his age

entries.rationale: Height far below peers.

entries.label: Small hand

source.sourcePhrase: His hands and feet are small

entries.rationale: Direct description.

entries.label: Genu valgum

source.sourcePhrase: his knees angle inward

entries.rationale: Knock-knees; inward-angled knees is the lay description of genu valgum.

entries.label: Genu valgum

source.sourcePhrase: his knees angle inward

entries.rationale: Standard lay name for the same finding (HPO synonym 'Knock knees').

entries.label: Proteinuria

source.sourcePhrase: protein and blood in my urine

entries.rationale: Literal meaning of proteinuria.

entries.label: Proteinuria

source.sourcePhrase: urine tests have kept showing sugar and protein

entries.rationale: Same finding, third person.

entries.label: Hematuria

source.sourcePhrase: protein and blood in my urine

entries.rationale: Literal meaning of hematuria.

entries.label: Tremor

source.sourcePhrase: a very slight shaking in my hands

entries.rationale: Involuntary shaking is tremor.

entries.label: Tremor

source.sourcePhrase: his hands shake

entries.rationale: Same finding, different wording.

entries.phrase: rings around the edge of my corneas
entries.label: Kayser-Fleischer ring

source.sourcePhrase: brownish rings around the edge of my corneas

entries.rationale: A brownish ring at the corneal edge is the description of a Kayser-Fleischer ring.

entries.label: Febrile seizure (within the age range of 3 months to 6 years)

source.sourcePhrase: seizure with a fever at 13 months

entries.rationale: Seizure with fever in a young child. Only valid for ages 3 months to 6 years, per the HPO name.

entries.label: Seizure

source.sourcePhrase: he had frequent seizures

entries.rationale: Direct use of the term.

entries.label: Seizure

source.sourcePhrase: had a fit when he was three

entries.rationale: 'Fit' is common British lay usage for a seizure.

entries.label: Hypopigmented skin patches

source.sourcePhrase: several pale patches on his chest, belly and back

entries.rationale: Pale skin patches are hypopigmented patches. The article calls them macules (HP:0020073); a lay phrase cannot tell size, so the broader patch term is used.

entries.label: Cognitive impairment

source.sourcePhrase: has struggled to think and count

entries.rationale: Difficulty thinking is cognitive impairment.

entries.label: Personality changes

source.sourcePhrase: his personality has changed

entries.rationale: Direct match.

entries.label: Unsteady gait

source.sourcePhrase: He can no longer walk steadily

entries.rationale: Only valid in a negated context ('cannot walk steadily'); the baseline extractor does not handle negation, see limitations.

entries.label: Hyperhidrosis

source.sourcePhrase: He sweats a lot

entries.rationale: Excessive sweating is hyperhidrosis.

entries.label: Constipation

source.sourcePhrase: is constipated

entries.rationale: Direct match.

entries.label: Glycosuria

source.sourcePhrase: urine tests have kept showing sugar and protein

entries.rationale: Literal meaning of glycosuria.

entries.label: Glycosuria

source.sourcePhrase: urine tests have kept showing sugar and protein

entries.rationale: Only valid when the context is a urine test, as in the source sentence.

entries.label: Aminoaciduria

source.sourcePhrase: extra amino acids in his urine

entries.rationale: Literal meaning of aminoaciduria.

entries.label: Hypouricemia

source.sourcePhrase: a low uric acid level in his blood

entries.rationale: Literal meaning of hypouricemia.

entries.phrase: tiny crystals in the clear front part of his eyes
entries.label: Corneal crystals

source.sourcePhrase: tiny crystals in the clear front part of his eyes

entries.rationale: The clear front part of the eye is the cornea. The lay phrase cannot specify cystine, so the general term is used.

entries.label: Motor delay

source.sourcePhrase: walked at fifteen months, a little later than other children

entries.rationale: Only valid together with 'later than other children'; walking at 15 months alone is within the normal range. Weak entry, kept as an example of a context-dependent phrase.

entries.label: Growth delay

source.sourcePhrase: she stopped growing as she should

entries.rationale: Growth below the expected rate.

entries.label: Joint stiffness

source.sourcePhrase: her joints became stiff

entries.rationale: Direct match.

entries.label: Joint stiffness

source.sourcePhrase: her joints became stiff

entries.rationale: Same finding, different word order.

entries.label: Lower limb pain

source.sourcePhrase: her legs hurt

entries.rationale: Pain in the legs.

entries.label: Coarse facial features

source.sourcePhrase: her facial features look coarse

entries.rationale: Direct match.

entries.label: Irritability

source.sourcePhrase: has been fussy and cranky

entries.rationale: Lay words for an irritable infant.

entries.label: Hypercalcemia

source.sourcePhrase: Blood tests showed far too much calcium

entries.rationale: Only valid for a blood test, as in the source sentence; urine calcium would be hypercalciuria.

entries.label: Nephrocalcinosis

source.sourcePhrase: a kidney scan showed calcium deposits

entries.rationale: Only valid when the context is the kidney, as in the source sentence. The general term is used because the lay phrase cannot specify the medulla.

entries.phrase: head size are all well below
entries.label: Microcephaly

source.sourcePhrase: his weight, length and head size are all well below the charts

entries.rationale: Head size well below the growth charts is microcephaly.

entries.label: Global developmental delay

source.sourcePhrase: He is far behind other children in using his hands, talking and getting along with people

entries.rationale: Delay across several developmental areas.
